components.gap: Only two instances are stated (densities on a bounded interval [A,B] with one mean constraint; a finite outcome set with no constraint beyond normalization). The general method's sample space with its reference measure, the declared constraint functions with their prescribed expectations, and the resulting feasible set of distributions are not stated, so the worked distribution is not shown to solve a declared general optimization problem.

The optimizer, its existence and uniqueness are derived only for the single-mean bounded-interval case and the finite unconstrained case. The general optimizer under declared constraints (exponential form relative to the reference measure) is not derived, and its existence/uniqueness qualifications (feasibility, constraint values in the interior of the attainable set, failure of existence or attainment, dependence on the reference measure) are not stated or proved.

The multiplier and normalizer are explained only for one constraint on a bounded interval (Z(lambda), monotone mean map, unique lambda). A general account of the multipliers and the normalization Z(lambda) for several declared constraints, without assuming that a feasible optimizer exists (including when no multiplier vector matches the declared constraint values), is not supplied.

Jaynes's normative inferential argument for maximum entropy and its premises (the entropy measure of uncertainty and its justification, maximum entropy as the least-committal assignment consistent with the given information, the conditions on what counts as given information, and the paper's stated statistical-mechanical application boundaries) is not reconstructed anywhere on the route; the handbook only names Jaynes as an advocate. The source is held (Jaynes 1957, Phys. Rev. 106) but no locator into it appears in the handbook.

A changed-constraint contrast (uniform on the bounds versus the fixed-mean entropy maximizer for the guide's 16.40/16.52/16.92 copper coefficient) and a representation-dependence example (factory cubes uniform in side, area or volume) are present, but no worked distribution is computed for the changed problem (the multiplier and the resulting density/variance for the guide's values are not given), and the reference-measure example is an indifference example rather than a worked maximum-entropy problem solved under two declared reference measures with the evidential warrant separated from the optimization.
